outcomes: One contributor offering distributes canonical skills and worker profiles; publication, language evaluation, load sampling and tree verification use native Go CLI commands
Contributor workflows reach tasks, proposals and memory through the providers the workspace binds, so a backend changes without a skill edit
A repository states its labels, states, worker profiles, language rule and publication defaults once, in its own configuration

Only build, spec, design, prototype, review, adr and check remain as workflow entries, alongside the configured explicit-only content-bump utility; legacy aliases and duplicated orchestration are removed
Build coordinates a requested intention, multi-task issue or epic from observable delivery units through its mandated stage, making demonstrated results, blockers and next actions visible
Material specs, designs, prototypes, ADRs and delivery boundaries receive independent challenge before adoption, with original findings and supported resolutions preserved
Versioned local records carry exact native artifact, handoff and producer references across sessions without creating another requirement registry or controller
nonGoals: Choosing a tasks, proposals or memory provider for the workspace, or falling back to another one
Authorizing publication, merge or deployment: the mandate and the repository's controls still decide
Changing host permissions, credentials or model access, which stay with the workspace and the host
Changing the separately owned audit workflow; its active language relay delegates to the shared native evaluator
Migrating other workspaces' separate agentArtifacts declarations and pins

requirements.text: One content-only @putnami/contributor extension ships build, spec, design, prototype, review, adr and check, the explicit content-bump utility, four worker profiles and shared references for both hosts. Build owns one planning/implementation/review/repair/check loop and continues until the requested outcome, concrete blocker or mandate boundary. A workspace opts in with extension:@putnami/contributor.

The configured content-bump utility is explicit-only on both hosts. Canonical workflows remain implicitly available for the requested objective. Implicit selection grants no backlog processing, task mutation, Git publication, merge or deployment authority; local implementation checkpoints remain within the authorized work.

Only canonical workflow entries and active configured utilities are materialized. Removed plan, execute, fix, epic, code-review, fix-loop and putnami-* entries have no metadata, resource directories or duplicate implementations. Unchanged owned legacy files are removed during upgrade; edited files remain protected and their collision is explicit.

No shipped file invokes a backend client, names a tracker label, a hosted repository address, a private memory identity or storage layout, or this repository's identity. Skills reach tasks, proposals and memory through putnami tasks, proposals or memory operations, or the matching MCP tools.

Native proposals finalize consumes a current native dossier or explicitly waits for named hosted checks; it executes no local gate. It pushes and publishes through bound contracts with exact readback and checked preconditions. Partial delivery preserves the opaque parent identity without closing or delivered transition. Draft seeds carry no closing directive. Unresolved writes stop without retry. Native language task scanning uses the tasks contract.

options["@putnami/contributor"] holds task sources, claimed/delivered states, tier labels and worker profiles, language/publication controls and active integrations. Removed backlog/filter/rank/plan-label settings have no canonical consumer. Instructions name profiles; host metadata supplies the model mapping.

A proposal opens as a draft before edits without a gate; an empty seed contains the title only. Its title/body form the squash message. Native finalization checks paragraph/body limits, English and attribution, posting proof as a comment. Build selects one final local or hosted gate from policy/load. The finalizer reuses the supplied native proof or waits for explicit named hosted checks on the pushed HEAD, returning to draft on failure.

The local workflow binds Git-tracked native manifests/specs and safe exact refs. Real native checks and corroborated cache provenance establish acceptance. Attained stages satisfy earlier required stages only with valid receipts. Current nonsuperseded material artifacts need challenge; later artifacts do not block current readiness. Original findings, entry conditions, experiment limits, decisions and handoffs remain visible. Progress grants no authority.

Both hosts install canonical source/package content with exact resource links, one build recipe index, repeat-install idempotence and edited-file protection. Legacy workflows and shell implementations are deleted; the active audit language relay only calls the native evaluator. Workflow records require advertised native support. Stage changes, reviews, adapters and publication rechecks never execute another gate; actual released adoption is distinct.
